entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 115:1-18 . The Psalmist prays that God would vindicate His glory, which is contrasted with the vanity of idols, while the folly of their worshippers is contrasted with the trust of God's people, who are encouraged to its exercise and to unite in the praise which it occasions.

entries.heading: 2. Where is now,
entries.text: 2. Where is now, &c.--"now" is "not a particle of time, but of entreaty," as in our forms of speech, "Come now," "See now," &c.

entries.heading: 7. speak . . . throat
entries.text: 7. speak . . . throat --literally, "mutter," not even utter articulate sounds.

entries.heading: 8. every one that trusteth
entries.text: 8. every one that trusteth --they who trust, whether makers or not.
14. Opposed to the decrease pending and during the captivity.
15-17. They were not only God's peculiar people, but as living inhabitants of earth, assigned the work of His praise as monuments of divine power, wisdom, and goodness.
18. Hence let us fulfil the purpose of our creation, and evermore show forth His praise.
